tasks.title: Lecture #13
tasks.instruction: Listen to a teacher talking in a social studies class.
tasks.transcript:
Have you ever thought about the games that people played hundreds of years ago? In the Middle Ages, people often got together and competed in various folk games. They would form teams and kick around a ball or some round object. The objective of a folk game was most often to move the ball to some fixed point and score points. Sounds a lot like modem games, doesn’t it? But in actuality, folk games were much different !
One big difference is that nowadays the rules of such games are written down. Each game has a specific clear set of rules that you can look up and consult when you’re not sure what to do. In the past, though, very few people who played these games could even read. So they simply memorized the rules and passed them down by tradition.
Also, the teams that played in folk games were nothing like the carefully structured teams in today’s games. Today，each player has a specific role. Like in soccer, when one player’s job is to protect the goal, and others try to score. There's a lot of specialization in roles and positions. But in the past, folk games were played more like children play games today. Think about how kids usually play a game: they will often change positions or roles. This is more or less how teams were organized in the past.
And another difference, nowadays, sports games are considered very positive activities. They keep you healthy and they teach teamwork. But folk games of the past were not regarded so positively. They were often played in the streets, and to a lot of people, they looked more like scary riots than sport events! The games were very rowdy and often ended in broken windows or other damage to property. In fact, folk games were considered so primitive that authorities in some places even tried to ban them completely. For example, in medieval England, authorities tried up to 30 times to stop such contests from being organized. But it didn't work. People continued to play these games in the streets for hundreds of years.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.C: How folk games were played in the past
options.D: When the rules of folk games were invented

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：这段讲话的主题是什么？ 定位原文： Have you ever thought about the games that people played hundreds of years ago? In the Middle Ages, people often got together and competed in various folk games. ... But in actuality, folk games were much different! One big difference is that nowadays the rules of such games are written down. ... Also, the teams that played in folk games were nothing like the carefully structured teams in today’s games. ... And another difference, nowadays, sports games are considered very positive activities. ... But folk games of the past were not regarded so positively. 选项分析： A. Who played folk games（谁玩民间游戏）。讲话虽提到人们组队参与，但并未重点讨论参与者的身份，所以A选项错误。 B. Why folk games disappeared（为什么民间游戏消失了）。讲话提到民间游戏持续了数百年，并未讨论其消失，所以B选项错误。 C. How folk games were played in the past（过去民间游戏是如何进行的）。讲话从规则、团队组织、社会看法等多个方面对比古今差异，描述了民间游戏的进行方式，因此C选项正确。 D. When the rules of folk games were invented（民间游戏的规则是什么时候发明的）。基于讲话未讨论规则发明的时间，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about the rules of folk games?

options.C: They have not changed over time.
options.D: They gave rise to rules of modem games.

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：演讲者对民间游戏的规则有什么暗示？ 定位原文： One big difference is that nowadays the rules of such games are written down. Each game has a specific clear set of rules that you can look up and consult when you’re not sure what to do. In the past, though, very few people who played these games could even read. So they simply memorized the rules and passed them down by tradition. 选项分析： A. They were not written down（它们没有被写下来）。讲话指出过去玩这些游戏的人大多不识字，规则靠记忆和传统口耳相传，暗示规则并未以文字形式记录，因此A选项正确。 B. They were hard to remember（它们很难记住）。基于讲话并未说明规则难以记忆，所以B选项错误。 C. They have not changed over time（它们随时间没有改变）。讲话未讨论规则的变化情况，所以C选项错误。 D. They gave rise to rules of modern games（它们催生了现代游戏的规则）。讲话对比古今差异，但未说明现代规则源自民间游戏，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention children's games?

options.A: To describe how teams were structured in folk games
options.B: To question whether children took part in folk games
options.C: To argue that young players are much better than adults
options.D: To suggest that watching folk games was family entertainment

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：演讲者为什么提到儿童游戏？ 定位原文： But in the past, folk games were played more like children play games today. Think about how kids usually play a game: they will often change positions or roles. This is more or less how teams were organized in the past. 选项分析： A. To describe how teams were structured in folk games（为了描述民间游戏的团队是如何组织的）。讲话明确用儿童游戏中经常换位置或角色的特点，类比过去民间游戏的团队组织方式，因此A选项正确。 B. To question whether children took part in folk games（为了质疑儿童是否参与民间游戏）。基于讲话并未质疑儿童的参与，所以B选项错误。 C. To argue that young players are much better than adults（为了论证年轻运动员比成年人好得多）。讲话未比较儿童与成年运动员的水平，所以C选项错误。 D. To suggest that watching folk games was family entertainment（为了表明观看民间游戏是家庭娱乐）。讲话未提及观看游戏与家庭娱乐的关系，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What did authorities in some places attempt to do?

options.B: Introduce clear rules for some games
options.C: Encourage children to practice for games
options.D: Prevent people from participating in games

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：一些地方的当局试图做什么？ 定位原文： In fact, folk games were considered so primitive that authorities in some places even tried to ban them completely. For example, in medieval England, authorities tried up to 30 times to stop such contests from being organized. 选项分析： A. Organize international contests（组织国际比赛）。基于讲话未提及组织比赛，所以A选项错误。 B. Introduce clear rules for some games（为某些游戏引入明确的规则）。讲话未提到当局制定规则，所以B选项错误。 C. Encourage children to practice for games（鼓励儿童为游戏练习）。由于讲话讨论的是禁止而非鼓励，所以C选项错误。 D. Prevent people from participating in games（阻止人们参与游戏）。讲话明确指出当局试图完全禁止民间游戏，多次阻止此类比赛的举办，因此D选项正确
